title: Polymer type and leaching conditions govern the yield and composition of dissolved organic matter released from microplastics
content: Microplastics can release dissolved organic matter (DOM), potentially influencing environmental quality and ecosystem health. However, the yields and molecular composition of microplastics-derived DOM (MPs-DOM) under different leaching conditions remain poorly characterized. This study investigates the polymer- and leaching-condition-dependent release of MPs-DOM, including its yield and composition, from microplastics, polyvinyl chloride (PVC), nylon-66 (NYL), and biodegradable polyhydroxyalkanoate (PHA), under water-soaking (WS), thermal leaching (TH), and UV-irradiation (UV). DOM release was strongly polymer- and treatment-dependent. Under WS, PVC exhibited the highest CDOM and DOC yields with apparent production rate of 207.8 m−1 h−1 and 10.72 ppm h−1, whereas NYL showed the lowest DOM yields and production rate (0.44 m−1 h−1 for CDOM and 1.16 ppm h−1 for DOC). Under UV irradiation, PHA exhibited the highest DOM yields, with DOC increasing from 13.5 to 802 ppm and CDOM from 26.5 to 533.9 m−1, and production rates (7.81 m−1 h−1 for CDOM and 12.13 ppm h−1 for DOC, respectively). PVC-derived DOM exhibited the greatest aromaticity (SUVA254 up to 0.103 L mg−1 m−1), whereas NYL-derived DOM showed the lowest (0.0002–0.0016 L mg−1 m−1). EEM-PARAFAC analysis identified protein-like, humic-/fulvic-like, and microbial byproduct-like fluorescent components, which are distinct among the three MPs-DOM pools. During prolonged UV exposure, PVC-DOM shifted from humic-/fulvic-like dominance (∼63%) to protein-like dominance (∼80%). PHA-DOM molecular size decreased during leaching, from 688 to 408 nm under WS, 997 to 459 nm under TH, and 514 to 336 nm under UV. Seawater slightly suppressed PVC-DOM release during WS but increased CDOM release under TH and UV to 16.2 and 217 m−1, respectively. These findings demonstrate that polymer type, leaching conditions, and salinity influence the yield and characteristics of MPs-DOM.
